Their lengths are 2→1→0; [F1] and the A2 supplier [F1] give precisely these covers, so each of the four vertices has undirected degree two and there are exactly two saturated paths.

Second vertices are w0, s1s2, s2s1, s1. Exactly w0→s1s2, w0→s2s1, s1s2→s1, s2s1→s1 are drawn. Their lengths are 3→2→1; local [F1] and the A2 supplier [F1] justify all four covers and no extra arrow is asserted.

The Remarks legend identifies each downward x→y arrow with ε(x,y)ι_{x→y}: M(x∘λ)→M(y∘λ), agreeing with local [F2] and def-bgg-differential-from-signed-verma-maps. Each of the eight labels has exactly its drawn endpoints as epsilon arguments; none specifies a numerical signing.

For each middle m, ι_{m→y}∘ι_{x→m} has domain M(x∘λ) and codomain M(y∘λ). Local [F2] and lem-bruhat-covers-give-unique-verma-embeddings proof 2.1 identify both composites with the same transported inclusion ι_{x→y}; this uses the existing coherent normalization, not arbitrary rescaled embeddings.

Put P1=ε(x,m1)ε(m1,y) and P2=ε(x,m2)ε(m2,y). By local [F3], P1P2=-1 and P1,P2∈{±1}, hence P2=-P1 and (P1+P2)ι_{x→y}=0. With (x,y)=(s1s2,e) this is Verification 2.1, and with (x,y)=(w0,s1) it is Verification 2.2. The figures do not assert that the signed path composites are equal. The original rigorous verification is untouched and independent of the figures.
